defects.detail: opening fragment 'schlossenen Gesamtheit des eigenen Nachdenkens fußen, fehlt es' rendered 'to find based on a closed totality...' with an unsupported 'to find'
note glosses 'Weltfrauen' as women living a religious life outside the cloister; source simply means laywomen/secular women

reason: Fourteen visions, songs, poems, letters to nuns and Weltfrauen, Brabant Dietsch and Ruisbroeck all rendered = source; only the mid-word opening fragment is slightly padded.

defects.detail: 'יצחק הדם' rendered 'he will laugh [at] the blood' and 'הפסח' as 'the remaining of the Passover' - literal word-for-word readings of garbled OCR yielding nonsense
colophon 'ובתהלתו שלם ספר הפרקים' split as 'with its praise, the book is completed / The Chapters of the Author' rather than 'with His praise the Book of Chapters is completed'

reason: Heavily corrupt OCR of Maimonides' Pirkei Moshe; translation is a literal, non-fluent word-by-word rendering that follows the OCR without papering over it, so most of the body is unreadable but recoverable; colophon correct in substance. Weak confidence in the garbled Hebrew.

defects.detail: 'felle recenti aſionis' (horned owl, explained by the next sentence on owls with ear-feathers) rendered 'fresh bile of a sea-fish'
'adeps foricis' (shrew) rendered 'fat of a burned dormouse'
'additis duabus sextis denarij sextini' rendered 'two-sixths of a sextarius of a denarius'

reason: Pliny's eye and head remedies rendered faithfully throughout; slips on asio (owl -> 'sea-fish'), sorex (-> 'dormouse') and the denarius fraction.

defects.detail: the entries for 三屋川 (source Taka-yama, flows into Hii River), 須佐川 (source Kotobiki-yama, through three districts into Kamado) and 磐鈕川 (source Ya-yama) are absent; only a stray 'Fish: Present.' remains
卑解/解 rendered as 'Hikage-no-kazura clubmoss' and 'Hige beard grass'; 薯蕷 transliterated 'Shōyu'

reason: Mountains, plant list, birds and beasts, and the Hata and Iishi streams = source, but three of the five river entries (Miya, Susa, Iwasusu) are dropped.

defects.detail: 'Talásyamtiwa' respelled 'Talássyamtiwa'

reason: English source lightly paraphrased; all six songs' actions and both footnotes (moved inline as notes) preserved = source.

defects.detail: source is a German page on Podagra (Nymphaea alba, Book XII, causes of gout: blood, bile, phlegm, black bile); translation is Achmet's dream book on rings, crowns, earrings and nuptials (Chapter 128)
the dream-interpretation passage is given twice in near-identical form

reason: Translation is of a different text entirely (Achmet's Oneirocritica) with none of the source's gout content.

defects.detail: bare footnote markers after 'Hermogenes medicus <gloss>2</gloss>, Hirfos <gloss>3</gloss>, Donasties <gloss>4</gloss>...' replaced by invented glosses, e.g. Hermogenes 'Likely referring to Hermes Trismegistus', Donasties 'A name associated with ancient esoteric knowledge'
'nec inveniebantur usquequaque' (were not found anywhere) rendered 'not found everywhere'

reason: Body of Secretum secretorum ch. 27 and 'De gloria inestimabili' = source, footnote on periodus correctly placed; the numbered name markers are filled with speculative invented identifications.
Collegium sanctum of 70 elders, Esdras's 70 books dictated by an angel, wisdom ending with Zacharias = source; nothing wrong found.

defects.detail: '司謁於德成閣外以元景夏所達於東宮之皇壇頌特給於承旨' (the palace attendant outside Deokseong-gak handed the ode to the secretary) rendered 'Through a messenger... the King gave... the Ode'
'吉甫作頌' rendered 'Jibo composing an ode' (Yin Jifu / Gilbo); '自比於古人' softened to 'follows the intent of the ancients'

reason: Spirit-throne covering dialogue (white vs blue flowered silk, oiled paper) and the Ode episode = source; minor slips on who handed over the ode and the Jifu allusion.
Defence of Greek study, the misellenes, Horace quote, Terminus, Biblia/Evangelia, theopneustos (2 Tim 3:16), medical and legal Greek terms all = source; nothing wrong found.

defects.detail: the three Lucretius verse lines 'frigore, cum summo gelidi cubat aequore saxi, / urgerive superne obtritum pondere terrae. / Iam iam non domus accipiet te laeta neque uxor' are absent
added note 'A woodcut shows the contrast between the burial of the wealthy... and the poor' - the source has no woodcut

reason: Italian commentary on III 875-928 rendered faithfully, but the Lucretius text lines are dropped and an invented woodcut description is added.

defects.detail: 'Párvulus Fílius hódie natus est nobis' rendered 'A little child is born to us this day', dropping 'Son'

reason: Christmas collect, Lauds antiphons, Heb. 1 capitulum, responsory and 'A solis ortus cardine' = source; only 'Filius' dropped.

defects.detail: apparatus readings rendered into English ('Dindorf ὥρασ'' -> 'to the seasons'), obscuring the Greek variants

reason: Lysistrata 1030-1037 and the Latin commentary (gnat/Tricorythus pun, Carystians, Philocleon, Ecclesiazusae) and footnotes = source; apparatus translated awkwardly but not wrongly.

defects.detail: source is on the Athenian Sicilian expedition (Nicias, Lamachus, Alcibiades, Taranto, Reggio, Catania); translation is an alchemical passage on dew, celestial fire and living gold citing 'Raymondo Lullio'

reason: Translation is of an entirely different text; none of the source's names or events appear.

defects.detail: 'mit allen heiligen Engeln und seelen' rendered 'angels and spirits' (souls)

reason: Love of Christ, the rope thrown from the wild sea, rejoicing over a reborn soul, grief for the lost = source.
